chunks: ʿAlī, from his father, from al-Nawfalī, from al-Sakūnī, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:
The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم said: “The well is without liability, the mute beast is without liability, and the mine is without liability.”

key_terms.الْعَجْمَاءُ: a dumb animal; an animal without speech
key_terms.الْمَعْدِنُ: a mine or mineral excavation site
key_terms.جُبَارٌ: not subject to compensation or liability for resulting harm

ai.seo_question: What does the hadith 'The well, the animal, and the mine are jubar' mean in Islamic law?
ai.summary: This hadith states a legal principle concerning cases in which harm or loss is not subject to financial liability. It identifies a well, an animal without speech, and a mine as categories in which resulting damage is treated as uncompensated under the stated rule.
